cleanup.notes: Setup creates the virtual environment .venv in the lab folder (the README creates it with python3 -m venv on macOS and Linux and py -m venv on Windows, as the modules page teaches, then activates it before the setup command; the prerequisite check is python3 --version on macOS and Linux and py --version on Windows, as the README says) and installs the exact versions pinned in starter/requirements.txt, which is the lab's lock of every installed package. The test command writes .pytest_cache and __pycache__ folders; starter/.pytest_cache appears only if the learner runs pytest inside starter, and the README's cleanup removes it. The Task 9 and Task 10 checks start child Python processes with bytecode writing off and the pytest cache plugin disabled, and those processes write nothing else. The lab uses no database, network or fixture files; the sample records live in starter/signups/sample.py. Resetting the learner's work means copying the three edited files back from a fresh copy of the lab. The expected output replaces the per-learner test count and the run time with placeholders, because Task 10 adds the learner's own tests to the run; pytest runs the learner's file before tests/test_main.py. The 55-minute median is a task-by-task authoring estimate of setup and the ten tasks (about 25 minutes on S14 and 30 on S15, inside each day's 20 + 40 minute coding-lab blocks), not a measured learner pilot; 60 minutes is the cap of the 30-60 minute module-lab allowance. Every task is behaviour-tested. Source checks add the taught construct where behaviour cannot show it: elif and while (Task 1), a for loop and an is None test (Task 2), the default value and type hints by signature (Task 3), *values and **fields by signature (Task 4), dict.get and items() unpacking (Task 5), the three comprehensions (Task 6), import logging and try/except ValueError/else/finally (Task 8), and import sys, a from-import of the learner's own signups.records module, a keyword call of session_status in the opposite order to its parameters and * and ** unpacking at the report_line call (Task 9). Task 7 and the __name__ guard are checked by behaviour only. Task 10 checks the learner's file for a fixture used by a parametrized test of at least 3 cases and a pytest.raises block, runs the learner's tests against their code and against four broken versions of session_status and parse_seats. Learner files are parsed from bytes, so a UTF-8 byte-order mark is accepted. Objectives practised but not claimed: the venv and requirements-file objectives (modules-imports-and-virtual-environments#o2, #o3) are practised in Setup, which no test can observe from inside the environment; writing-and-running-script-files#o1's terminal run and exit-status reading is asked for in Task 9 and observed only through the subprocess checks of the same script; predict-and-explain objectives are left to the topic pages.
